title: Sampled traffic duplication with tenant fencing and cost telemetry
creator: Miguel Torres
description: Goal: implement a production-safe traffic duplication pipeline that allows running production requests against evaluation or canary model endpoints without impacting production SLOs or tenant billing. Key features: (1) deterministic per-tenant sampled duplication using token-bucket budgets, (2) strict tenant fencing so duplicated requests cannot consume tenant KV cache or write billing-affecting artifacts, (3) per-duplication cost telemetry and internal chargeback, (4) automatic rollback triggers based on latency/error/cost regressions, and (5) audit trail + opt-out controls for sensitive customers. This ticket covers design, gateway changes, sampling engine, cost accounting hooks, and rollout/runbook.
comments: 2025-07-03 - Initial design doc linked: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/ModelLifecycle/duplication-sampling-design (proto draft). High-level architecture: gateway interceptor -> sampling decision -> duplication router -> isolated evaluation pool. Action: prototype sampling engine in gateway-proxy repo.

2025-07-07 - Implementation note: will stamp duplicated requests with header 'x-duplication-mode: sampled-eval' and 'x-duplication-budget-id: <tenant-id>-<bucket>'. This instructs downstream runtime to bypass tenant KV cache and route model outputs into isolated telemetry buckets. Engineering decision to avoid full request deep-copying in the gateway; instead forward a minimal metadata-backed pointer and let runtime fetch request body from fast-safe-store when needed.

2025-07-09 - Trade-offs discussed in review: (a) bypassing KV cache for duplicated traffic preserves production cache quality but underestimates some model behaviors tied to context; (b) allowing a read-only KV-shadow would increase fidelity but complicate isolation and billing. Decided on strict no-cache access for Phase 1 with metric instrumentation to measure divergence.

2025-07-11 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway-proxy/pull/482. Changes: sampling index, per-tenant token-bucket controller, duplication headers, and telemetry emitters (duplicated_tokens, duplicated_requests, duplication_cost_cents). Assigned reviewers: @saikat, @emma-r.

2025-07-13 - QA plan: run end-to-end tests in staging with synthetic tenants across three profiles (low-cost, bursty, high-QPS). Validate 0 impact on production latency by running high load with duplication enabled. Tests to assert isolation: duplicated requests must not create persisted entries in tenant namespaces. Add unit tests for token-bucket refill and overflow behavior.

2025-07-14 - Rollout plan: phased enablement. Step 0: internal-only (redwood internal org) at 100% sampling but strict budget. Step 1: opt-in customers flagged by solutions engineering at 0.1% global traffic. Step 2: increase to 1% then 5% for selected tenants. Step 3: general availability with tenant-default budget 0.05% and admin opt-in. Each step gated by acceptance criteria (see acceptance checklist comment).

2025-07-15 - Acceptance checklist: (1) duplication_rate metric matches configured sample fraction within 10% at multiple QPS levels, (2) production p50/p95 latency delta < 3ms at 99th percentile traffic during test window, (3) duplicated_tokens are attributed to internal cost center and visible in billing UI, (4) auto-rollback triggers correctly fire in simulated error injection tests.
Follow-ups: add adaptive sampling that increases sample rate for tenants showing model regressions during A/B experiments; integrate duplication telemetry with Optimize's cost recommendation engine.
